skill.name: skill-bootstrap
skill.description: Bootstrap a new agent skill — gather context, draft name/description/body, then create after confirmation.

attachment.anyPhrases: create a skill,create skill,create a new skill,new skill,add skill,bootstrap skill,draft a skill,help me write a skill,author a skill

skill.when_attached: - Follow this playbook immediately for the current request. - Never ask the user for description or content before running `` and ``. - Use provided name/module as draft defaults; infer the rest from context and tool results.
skill.skill_bootstrap_intent_routing:
1. BOOTSTRAP (bootstrap, help me write a skill, create a new skill, add a skill, draft a skill): - Follow the steps below in order. - Never call `create_skill` until the user explicitly confirms the draft. - If the user already supplies a complete name, description, and full body, skip to `skill-management` CREATE instead.
2. REVISE (change, update draft, tweak, add attachment): - Update the draft from feedback. - Re-present the draft for confirmation. - Do not call write tools until confirmed.
skill.collect_input: Gather from the user request and conversation history: - Goal: what workflow or task the skill should teach an agent to perform. - Target module: `finance`, `obsidian`, `configuration`, or an agent id that maps to one of these. - Triggers: phrases, cron job names, or routing cues that should auto-attach the skill. - Steps: ordered actions, tool calls, templates, constraints, and prohibited behavior. - Ask only for missing critical fields. Do not block drafting when enough context exists to produce a useful first draft.
skill.enrich_with_tools:
Use available tools to fill gaps before drafting. Skip calls that are not needed.
1. Resolve the owning agent and module: - Call `list_runtime_agents` when the target agent or module is unclear. - Call `preview_runtime_agent(id)` when full capability or prompt context is needed (configuration write access only; not available on `system-config-read`).
2. Resolve available tools for the target agent: - Call `list_capabilities` when the skill must reference specific agent tools. - Match capability ids to the target agent's configured capabilities.
3. Avoid duplication and learn existing patterns: - Call `list_skills(module)` for the target module. - Call `preview_skill(module, name)` on the closest existing skill to mirror structure, intent routing, and attachment style.
skill.generate_draft:
Produce all of the following:
1. `name`: concise kebab-case identifier; must not collide with an existing skill in the target module. 2. `description`: one catalog-facing line specific enough for routing and skill selection. 3. `content`: skill body only — do not include the root `` tag; `create_skill` sets `name`, `module`, and `description` on the root element.
Body guidelines: - Use numbered intent routing or ordered step sections like existing skills. - Name tools explicitly when the agent should call them. - Include `` only when trigger phrases or cron names are known. - Include templates, path rules, prohibited actions, and output expectations when relevant. - Keep the body concise and operational; avoid prose essays.
skill.present_draft:
Return the draft using the skill output template fields plus the body:
Module: [module] Skill Name: [name] Description: [description] Status: Draft
Then show the drafted body content for review. Ask the user to confirm, revise, or cancel.
skill.on_confirm: When the user explicitly confirms: - Call `create_skill(module, name, description, content)`. - Report using the skill output template with `Status: Created`.
skill.on_cancel: When the user cancels: - Do not call write tools. - Acknowledge cancellation without persisting anything.
